newsitem.title: UK: Britain urges war on poverty to mark millennium.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges war on poverty to mark millennium.

text.p: Britain called on Thursday for a renewed war on poverty to mark the new millennium and said it was adopting a new approach in its aid programmes.
International Development Secretary Clare Short, speaking at a conference in London, said poverty is the single greatest challenge the world faces but it can be eliminated in the next 50 years.
"I believe abject poverty could be eliminated from our world within our lifetime, or at least within the lifetime of our children," she said.
"Clearly there can be no more noble a task that the world could commit itself to as we approach a new millennium."

Short said Britain was committed to halving the proportion of people in extreme poverty by the year 2015, achieving equality for girls in education by 2005, assuring primary education in all countries by 2015 and achieving a cut in child mortality rates by 2015.

"Progress during the past 50 years in eliminating poverty has been greater than in the previous 500 years. We haven't done enough but much has been achieved and that achievement teaches us how to do the rest."
Rather than simply assisting developing nations, which she described as a "one-way charitable process", Short said Britain has now focused on working with them and forging partnerships.
"We are looking increasingly to develop partnerships and shared strategies for poverty reduction. We want to work as equals with governments," she said.
Short called for clarification about what development programmes are meant to do and said the interests of the poor should be taken into consideration when designing projects and setting strategies.
